name: Geetanjali Restaurant (OTDC)
area: Sun Temple Road, opposite the temple gate
signature_dish: Odia veg/non-veg thali with fish curry and rice
why_it_matters: Run by the Odisha Tourism Development Corporation and located directly in front of the Sun Temple as you exit the main gate — the default sit-down stop for the steady stream of temple visitors. It is the closest reliable full-meal option to the World Heritage monument itself, which otherwise has only carts and stalls. Tripadvisor 3.4/5 across roughly 10 reviews.
insider_tip: Come straight off the temple visit for a thali rather than hunting Konark town's thin restaurant strip — it is a two-minute walk from the gate. Government-run pricing means no tourist mark-up. Lunch is the busiest service; arrive before 1pm or after 2.30pm to avoid the tour-bus rush.
signature_address: Sun Temple Road, opposite Konark Sun Temple, Konark, Puri District, Odisha 752111

name: Kamat Restaurant
area: Konark town, near the Sun Temple
signature_dish: South Indian and North Indian vegetarian plates
why_it_matters: The most consistently rated sit-down restaurant in Konark town — Tripadvisor 4.3/5, the highest-rated full-service eatery near the Sun Temple. Part of the long-running Kamat chain known across Odisha for clean kitchens and reliable vegetarian food, which makes it the safe-stomach choice for travellers wary of roadside fare on a temple day-trip.
insider_tip: This is the dependable option if you want a proper meal before or after the temple rather than beach-shack seafood — it serves breakfast through dinner. Vegetarians get the widest menu here; the dosas and thalis are the staples. Cash and UPI accepted.
signature_address: Near Sun Temple, Konark, Puri District, Odisha 752111

name: Hotel Chandrabhaga & Restaurant
why_it_matters: Sits right on the corner where the Chandrabhaga Beach marine-drive road begins, roughly 3km from the Sun Temple — the most convenient sit-down meal for visitors pairing the temple with the beach. Tripadvisor 3.6/5 across about 25 reviews. The region's signature is Bengali-style fish fry, and the kitchen leans into seafood given the beach location.
insider_tip: Combine it with a Chandrabhaga Beach walk rather than treating it as a town restaurant — it is right at the beach turn-off. Fresh seafood depends on the morning catch, so ask what is in before ordering crab or prawn. Quieter than the temple-gate strip.
signature_address: Chandrabhaga Beach Road, Konark, Puri District, Odisha 752111

name: Nature Camp Konark Retreat Restaurant
signature_dish: Seafood and Indian dishes in a garden setting
why_it_matters: The in-house restaurant of Nature Camp Konark Retreat, an eco-tented property about 200m from the Sun Temple. Tripadvisor reviewers describe it as a calm break from the noise and chaos of the temple gate. It gives day-trippers a greener, quieter sit-down option than the busy roadside eateries, and the kitchen does both seafood and Odia plates.
insider_tip: Worth the short walk off the main temple road for the garden seating — a good spot to rest mid-day. As it is a small camp kitchen, call ahead if you want a full seafood spread rather than walk-in à la carte. Best for a relaxed late lunch.
signature_address: Nature Camp Konark Retreat, near Sun Temple, Konark, Puri District, Odisha 752111

name: Sun Temple Hotel & Restaurant
why_it_matters: A budget hotel-restaurant near the Konark bus stand serving Indian meals through two daily windows (roughly 8am-3.30pm and 6-10pm). It is one of the few documented eateries actually in Konark town centre rather than at the temple gate or beach, making it a practical stop for travellers arriving or leaving by bus.
insider_tip: Useful mainly for its location by the bus stand — handy if you are catching transport to Puri or Bhubaneswar. Note the split timings: there is a gap mid-afternoon. Prices are low; expect simple, no-frills cooking rather than a destination meal.
signature_address: Near Bus Stand, Konark, Puri District, Odisha 752111
